question.leadin: This monarch put down Pugachev's Rebellion, and her lover Grigory Orlov helped orchestrate a coup to overthrow her husband, Peter III.
question.text: Name this empress of Russia known as "the Great."
question.answerHtml: Catherine the Great [or Catherine II; or Yekaterina Velikaya; or Yekaterina Alekseevna; or Princess Sophie of Anhalt-Zerbst]
question.clue: This ruler placed Stanislaw Poniatowski on the throne of a neighboring nation, and one advisor to this ruler created namesake sham villages on the Crimean peninsula.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about leaders with titles in common.
swap.text: Give the title last held by Nicholas II of Russia before he was killed in 1918.
swap.clue: It's not in Germany, but one holder of this title issued the Anti-Semitic May Laws, which prohibited the creation of new towns by Jews.

question.text: Prior to the Bolshevik Revolution, Russia was briefly ruled by the Provisional government under this man, whose disastrous June Offensive led in part to the Bolshevik rise.
question.clue: A July 1917 operation named for this man was the last Russian offensive in World War One, commanded by Aleksei Brusilov.

swap.text: The "Secret Speech" was given by this successor to Stalin. During a meeting with the United Nations, this leader allegedly banged his shoe on a table in protest.
swap.clue: An action this leader is famous for occurred on their second, uninvited, visit to the US, during an October 12, 1960 speech by the Filipino delegate Lorenzo Sumulong.

question.text: After his 1982 death, Brezhnev was succeeded by this Russian leader. However, he died shortly thereafter from a host of diseases exacerbated by kidney failure.
question.clue: This man diplomatically wrote "we want peace" in order to be "growing wheat, building and inventing, writing books and flying into space" in his infamous letter to ten year old Samantha Smith.

swap.text: At Borodino, Matvei Platov led a regiment of these people in a cavalry charge against the French army. Ivan Mazepa led a detachment of the Zaporozhian ("zah-pohr-IJ-ian") group of these nomads during the Great Northern War.
swap.clue: A series of military campaigns in Poland called the "Deluge" occurred following an uprising of these people led by Bogdan Khmelnytsky ("k'mel-NIT-skee").

question.leadin: A huge cannon known as the Raevsky Redoubt formed a crucial part of the defender's line in this battle.
question.text: Mikhail Kutuzov led the Russian defense in this 1812 battle where Matvei Platov led a cossack charge against Eugene de Beauharnais. This battle was the single bloodiest day of the Napoleonic Wars.
question.clue: Pierre Bezhukov spends most of this battle in a battery at the Raevsky Redoubt, and Mikhael Kutusov is described as being inactive during it.

swap.leadin: The history of a state centered on this city was related in the Primary Chronicle traditionally attributed to Nestor.
swap.text: Yaroslav the Wise was once the grand prince of what city? Oleg of Novgorod founded a state named for this city that was ruled by the Rurikid dynasty.
swap.clue: A ruler of this city militarily supported the Byzantine emperor Basil II, which resulted in the formation of the Varangian Guard, in exchange for marrying Basil II's sister Anna.

question.text: This capital of the USSR was the site of the 1980 Olympics, as well as frequent "physical culture" parades in Red Square.
question.clue: This city traces its history to a post founded by Yuri of the Long Arm.

swap.leadin: Name these places associated with suicide bombers.
swap.text: In June 2003, a bus transporting pilots for the Russian Air Force was destroyed and fifteen were killed in the North Ossetia region, which borders this secessionist republic believed to be the source of the bomber.
swap.clue: Prior to 1991, this territory was combined with its western neighbor Ingushetia.

question.leadin: Winston Churchill called this country "a riddle, wrapped in a mystery, inside an enigma."
question.text: First, name this country, the largest to survive after the collapse of the U.S.S.R.
question.clue: The mostly-defunct political party Yabloko is a protest voice in this country.

swap.leadin: Name some things about the Golden Horde.
swap.text: Batu and Subotai's conquest of this state culminated in the 1223 Battle of the Kalka River. This state's Golden Age occurred under the reigns of Vladimir the Great and Yaroslav the Wise.
swap.clue: Its leaders used a system of succession in which the throne would pass to the eldest brother of the deceased, called the rota or "ladder" system.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the numerous successor states left behind by the Mongol Empire.
question.text: This successor state to the Golden Horde was founded by Haci I Giray. It was shown great deference by the Ottomans and was protected by them. In return, this state furnished Istanbul's markets with a great number of slaves taken from the steppes. This Khanate was conquered by Russia under Catherine the Great in 1783.
question.clue: Kabardia was made a nominal vassal of this state, while this state itself was removed from the Ottoman sphere of influence, by the Treaty of Kucuk Kaynarca ("koo-CHOOK kye-nar-JAH").

swap.text: Basil married his sister, Anna Porphyrogenita, to this man in return for military assistance. The Primary Chronicle is the source of an anecdote in which this man sent envoys to learn the religions of the world.
swap.clue: This Rurikid king, the father of Yaroslav the Wise, who used Old Church Slavonic for the Eastern Orthodox rites he converted to.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the man who was king of Poland until 1831.
question.text: The Russians attempted to relieve Sevastopol in this November 1854 battle, the last major Crimean War conflict before Nicholas's death, but the Sandbag Battery and some fog let the outnumbered British win.
question.clue: As was a theme for the larger war, poor British leadership, this time under by Lord Raglan, was partially ameliorated by English bravery.

swap.leadin: The racist colonel Grigory Zass collected the heads of these people to send to his friends.
swap.text: Name these people, whose twelve tribes include the Kabardy and Besleney. 95% of these people were killed or deported during a 19th-century genocide.
swap.clue: A dynasty of this ethnic group, which includes the Adyghe ("ah-dih-GAY") and Kabardians, replaced the Mamluk Dynasty's Turkic Bahri dynasty.

question.text: The story about Vladimir rejecting Islam because of its prohibition on alcohol comes from the Primary Chronicle, which was likely compiled by this monk who lived at the Monastery of the Caves. He also wrote a work called the Reading, about the murders of Boris and Gleb.

swap.leadin: This ruler reformed the poliudue system of tribute after their spouse was killed.
swap.text: Name this ruler whose spouse Igor was captured by the Drevelians while collecting tribute, tied to two birch trees, and killed. This ruler was succeeded by her son Sviatoslav ("Se-vit-to-slav") the Brave.
swap.clue: After receiving a request from Prince Mal, this ruler had negotiators carried to them in a boat and buried them alive.

question.leadin: Answer some stuff about a group of Russian soldiers, FTPE.
question.text: This elite class of musketeers engaged in a failed 1698 uprising against Peter the Great and was purged shortly afterwards.
question.clue: This group, which was initially armed with arquebuses, fought in the Siege of Kazan.

swap.leadin: Name these things about Alexander Scriabin's uncle, Vyacheslav Scriabin, FTP each.
swap.text: As a member of the Politburo Molotov was the key signatory, behind Beria, of the order that caused this execution of 25,000 Poles near the namesake area in 1940.
swap.clue: As head of the NKVD, Beria was responsible for masterminding this execution of captive Polish officers in the namesake site in 1940.
